title: Thinking About Divorce This Summer? Here’s What to Know

content.rendered:
Summer often brings major life changes. For many families, it can also become a time of reflection, transition, and difficult decisions about the future of a marriage. In fact, many couples begin considering divorce during the summer months after the school year ends and family routines begin to shift.

If you are thinking about divorce this summer, understanding your legal options early can help you feel more prepared and confident about the process ahead.

Let’s take a closer look at some important things to know.

Why Summer Is a Common Time for Divorce Discussions

Many couples postpone major family decisions until the school year is over in order to minimize disruptions for their children. Summer can provide additional flexibility for:

  • Scheduling consultations with a divorce attorney.
  • Discussing parenting arrangements.
  • Preparing for financial changes.
  • Planning for the upcoming school year.

For some families, the slower pace of summer also creates more time to evaluate ongoing marital issues and consider next steps.

While every situation is unique, summer often becomes a practical time for families to begin planning for change.

Understanding Divorce in Colorado

Colorado is a no-fault divorce state. This means that neither spouse is required to prove misconduct or wrongdoing in order to file for divorce.

Instead, the court focuses on whether the marriage has experienced an “irretrievable breakdown,” meaning the relationship can no longer be repaired.

Some important aspects of Colorado divorce law include:

  • A 91-day waiting period before a divorce can be finalized.
  • Division of marital property under equitable distribution laws.
  • Child custody decisions based on the best interests of the child.
  • Potential child support and spousal maintenance considerations.

Understanding these legal basics can help reduce uncertainty during an already emotional time.

Important Issues to Consider Before Filing for Divorce

Before beginning the divorce process, it is important to carefully evaluate several key areas that may impact your future.

Parenting Plans and Summer Schedules

If children are involved, summer schedules can become more complicated during divorce proceedings. Parents may need to discuss:

  • Vacation schedules.
  • Summer travel plans.
  • Camp activities.
  • Temporary parenting arrangements.

Clear communication and planning can help reduce stress for both parents and children.

Financial Preparation

Divorce can significantly impact finances, making preparation especially important. It may be helpful to:

  • Gather financial documents.
  • Review shared accounts and debts.
  • Understand household expenses.
  • Begin planning for separate living arrangements.

Being organized early can help make the process smoother moving forward.

Emotional Readiness

Divorce is not only a legal process — it is also a major emotional transition. Taking time to seek support from trusted friends, family members, or professionals can help individuals navigate the emotional challenges that often come with divorce.

How to Prepare for a Consultation With a Divorce Lawyer

Meeting with an experienced Colorado divorce attorney can help you better understand your rights, responsibilities, and legal options.

Before your consultation, consider gathering:

  • Basic financial information.
  • Questions about custody or parenting time.
  • Information regarding shared property or assets.
  • Any existing agreements or court documents.

The more prepared you are, the more productive your consultation may be.

Why Early Legal Guidance Matters

Even if you are still uncertain about divorce, obtaining legal information early can help you:

  • Understand your options.
  • Avoid common mistakes.
  • Prepare for future decisions.
  • Protect your rights and interests.

Having clarity early in the process often reduces stress and helps families move forward with greater confidence.
